arxiv-2111-08010.title: Modular Networks Prevent Catastrophic Interference in Model-Based Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2111-08010.creator: Robin Schiewer, Laurenz Wiskott
arxiv-2111-08010.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Robin Schiewer, Laurenz Wiskott. In a multi-task reinforcement learning setting, the learner commonly benefits from training on multiple related tasks by exploiting similarities among them. At the same time, the trained agent is able to solve a wider range of different problems. While this effect is well documented for model-free multi-task methods, we demonstrate a detrimental effect when using a single learned dynamics model for multiple tasks.

arxiv-2203-07251.title: The value of the early-time Lieb-Robinson correlation function for qubit arrays
arxiv-2203-07251.creator: Brendan J. Mahoney, Craig S. Lent
arxiv-2203-07251.description: Abstract The Lieb-Robinson correlation function captures propagation of quantum correlations in many-body system. We calculate the value of the leading order of the correlation function, not its bound, for a system of interacting qubits at early times. The general analytical result is compared to numerical calculations and is applied to regular qubit lattices in one, two, and three dimensions.

arxiv-2208-02325.title: Small changes at single nodes can shift global network dynamics
arxiv-2208-02325.creator: Kalel L. Rossi, Roberto C. Budzinski, Bruno R. R. Boaretto, Lyle E. Muller, Ulrike Feudel
arxiv-2208-02325.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kalel L. Rossi, Roberto C. Budzinski, Bruno R. R. Boaretto, Lyle E. Muller, Ulrike Feudel. Understanding the sensitivity of a system’s behavior with respect to parameter changes is essential for many applications. This sensitivity may be desired - for instance in the brain, where a large repertoire of different dynamics, particularly different synchronization patterns, is crucial - or may be undesired - for instance in power grids, where disruptions to synchronization may lead to blackouts.

arxiv-2304-05220.title: Solving the domain wall problem with first-order phase transition
arxiv-2304-05220.creator: Yang Li, Ligong Bian, Yongtao Jia
arxiv-2304-05220.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yang Li, Ligong Bian, Yongtao Jia. Domain wall networks are two-dimensional topological defects generally predicted in many beyond standard model physics. In this Letter, we propose to solve the domain wall problem with the first-order phase transition. We numerically study the phase transition dynamics, and for the first time show that the domain walls reached scaling regime can be diluted through the interaction with vacuum bubbles during the first-order phase transition.

arxiv-2411-03447.title: The evaporation of charged black holes
arxiv-2411-03447.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . Charged particle emission from black holes with sufficiently large charge is exponentially suppressed. As a result, such black holes are driven towards extremality by the emission of neutral Hawking radiation. Eventually, an isolated black hole gets close enough to extremality that the gravitational backreaction of a single Hawking photon becomes important, and the quantum field theory in curved spacetime approximation breaks down. To proceed further, we need to use a quantum theory of gravity.

arxiv-2501-08831.title: The post-gas expulsion coalescence of embedded clusters as an origin of open clusters
arxiv-2501-08831.creator: J. W. Zhou Sami Dib Pavel Kroupa
arxiv-2501-08831.description: Abstract The mismatch between the mass function of the Milky Way’s embedded clusters (ECs) and that of open clusters (OCs) raises the question of whether each OC originates from a single EC. In this work, we explore a scenario in which OCs form as a result of post-gas expulsion coalescence of ECs within the same parental molecular cloud.

arxiv-2506-02917.title: Text-guided Generation of Efficient Personalized Inspection Plans
arxiv-2506-02917.creator: Xingpeng Sun, Zherong Pan, Xifeng Gao, Kui Wu, Aniket Bera
arxiv-2506-02917.description: Abstract We propose a training-free, Vision-Language Model (VLM)-guided approach for efficiently generating trajectories to facilitate target inspection planning based on text descriptions. Unlike existing Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) methods designed for general agents in unknown environments, our approach specifically targets the efficient inspection of known scenes, with widespread applications in fields such as medical, marine, and civil engineering.

arxiv-2509-16762.title: Novel Bounds From The Weak Gravity and Festina Lente Conjectures
arxiv-2509-16762.creator: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Pratik Chattopadhyay, Nobuchika Okada, Roman Pasechnik, Zhi-Wei Wang
arxiv-2509-16762.description: Abstract We demonstrate that the Weak Gravity Conjecture (WGC) and the Festina-Lente Conjecture (FLC) yield novel bounds on fifth force searches and milli-Charged Particles (mCPs), as well as on the scale of inflation and on the effective Higgs quartic interaction.

arxiv-2601-02984.description: Abstract The aim of this work is to enhance blockchain security by deepening the understanding of selfish mining attacks in various consensus protocols, especially the ones that have the potential to mitigate selfish mining.
